prompt: A cart already holds $7$ pounds of equipment and can carry a total of no more than $40$ pounds. Each box loaded onto it weighs $3$ pounds. What is the greatest number of boxes that can be loaded onto the cart?

hints.text: $b \le 11$, so the greatest whole number of boxes is $11$.

learningObjective: Translate a capacity constraint into an inequality and interpret the result.
explanation: "No more than $40$" translates to $\le 40$. The total weight is $3b + 7$.
Boxes come in whole numbers, so the maximum is $11$. Check: $3(11) + 7 = 40$ ✓, exactly at the limit.

alternativeExplanations.title: Reason with the remaining capacity
steps: Of the $40$-pound limit, $7$ pounds is already used, leaving $33$ pounds.
When the division comes out even, the boundary value is achievable — "no more than" allows equality, so $11$ works rather than $10$.
